subject: Proposal: transient headroom charge cap and retrospective reconciliation
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmewidgets.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: support+billing@acmewidgets.com
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected Q4 spike — request for temporary headroom and smoothing

Hi Olga,

We had an unplanned campaign kickoff last week that drove a short burst of traffic through Redwood. We've attached the October usage export for visibility. Our billing shows an overrun that will blow past our committed monthly threshold by ~3.5x for a 48-hour window.

Before I submit a formal PO for increased committed capacity, can Redwood help in two ways: 1) a short-term "headroom" allowance with a capped surcharge so we don't get hit with a massive invoice, and 2) the ability to reconcile/true-up that surcharge across our next two invoices (smoothing).

If this is feasible, we also need a one-page amendment or term sheet we can attach to our procurement ticket. Time is tight — can we get a proposal by COB PT on Monday?

Thanks,
Jane Doe
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Widgets

Attachment: usage_report_october.csv (CSV, 38KB)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmewidgets.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected Q4 spike — request for temporary headroom and smoothing

Hi Jane — thanks for the heads-up and the export. We can definitely help with a limited transient headroom and amortized reconciliation. High-level options below; I've cc'd Rishi (AE) and Laura (Finance) to keep approvals in the loop.

Option A — Short buffer with capped surcharge (fastest):
- 72-hour headroom allocation equal to 4x baseline throughput.
- Capped surcharge of 1.25x list rate for tokens above committed thresholds during the headroom window.
- Surcharge is refundable as a credit spread across the next two invoices if Acme signs an amendment to increase committed capacity within 30 days.

Option B — Temporary uplift with fixed fee (procurement-friendly):
- 30-day temporary uplift to next tier (predictable unit rate).
- Fixed uplift fee invoiced once, with 50% applied as a credit toward the following monthly invoice.

We can provide a one-page term sheet for either option. Attached is a draft term sheet (temp_headroom_term_sheet.pdf) that maps to Option A. If you prefer Option B, we'll revise and send a version that finance can attach to the PO.

Next steps: pick option + confirm whether you want the surcharge refundable as a credit (requires amendment) or non-refundable (faster, no legal amendment). We can get a signed amendment to you within 48 hours if you want refundable credit.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: temp_headroom_term_sheet.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmewidgets.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: support+billing@acmewidgets.com
Date: 2026-10-18T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected Q4 spike — request for temporary headroom and smoothing

Thanks, Olga. Option A looks closest to what Procurement wants — predictable surcharge but refundable if we expand. Two clarifications before we escalate:
1) Can you confirm the cap applies per-token and not as a % of total invoice? We need line-level clarity for our FinOps team.
2) If we sign the amendment, will Redwood waive any short-window early-termination/Myriad surcharges? Procurement flags one-off fees.

If you can email a term sheet with those points called out, we'll route it to legal/finance and aim to sign quickly.

—Jane

Date: 2026-10-19T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: approval path for refundable headroom credit

Olga/Laura — quick internal note before we send the updated term sheet to Acme: Finance needs confirmation on two items for a refundable surcharge flow:
1) Minimum expansion commitment threshold (we typically require a +20% committed increase sustained for 3 months to apply full refund as credits). Is Acme likely to meet that?
2) Do we allow credit to be spread across two invoices only, or extend to three if the uplift payment timing misaligns?

My read from the account is that Acme is conservative; suggest we soften the expansion requirement to +15% for this one-time accommodation and allow credits over three invoices to make procurement happier. Laura — can finance sign off on that tradeoff?

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmewidgets.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected Q4 spike — request for temporary headroom and smoothing

Hi all — following internal review, Redwood is prepared to proceed with Option A with the following commercial clarifications, which we've captured in the attached amendment for signature: acme_docusign_amendment.docx

- Headroom window: 72 hours, as proposed.
- Surcharge: capped at 1.25x per-token list rate and applied at the token line item (not as % of invoice).
- Refundability: Refundable only if Acme increases committed capacity by at least 15% relative to the current committed baseline and sustains that new level for 2 consecutive full months.
- Credit application: Refundable surcharge will be applied as credits spread across up to 3 subsequent invoices to accommodate billing cycles.
- Waivers: Redwood will waive any short-window administrative setup fees associated with the headroom provisioning. Standard termination terms remain unchanged.

Please review the attached amendment. If agreeable, Jane — sign via the DocuSign link below and we'll mark the headroom active retrospectively for the Oct 12–14 spike window.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/link/ABC12345
HubSpot deal: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-Q4-SPK

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
